summary: Targeted re-test of pointer-events fix on .hero-bg (iteration_4 HIGH bug). Filled /kontakt form, submitted with a NORMAL click (no force), reached 'Vielen Dank!' success screen, clicked 'Neue Anfrage stellen' with a NORMAL click (no force) - it was fully clickable. Form re-appeared with consent unchecked and name field empty. Regression: submit CTA on /kontakt itself is a hero-area button and worked with normal click, confirming the pointer-events:none on .hero-bg only affects the decorative background, not real CTAs.
critical_code_review_comments: Home hero primary CTA element had a bounding box starting at x=1939 (outside 1920 viewport) during regression probe - likely a slider/carousel off-screen slide, not related to the pointer-events fix. Worth a quick manual check if a hero CTA is meant to be visible above the fold on '/'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_4 bug (reset button unclickable on /kontakt success screen due to .hero-bg overlay intercepting pointer events) is RESOLVED by adding pointer-events:none to .hero-bg. Verified with a normal .click() (no force). Full form reset works (consent unchecked, fields empty).
rca of the issue: RCA: The decorative .hero-bg absolutely-positioned element (inset:0) was layered above the hero content in stacking order and captured pointer events. Fix: pointer-events:none on .hero-bg lets clicks pass through to underlying buttons. Buttons themselves are unaffected because pointer-events is not inherited into siblings/children of other elements - only the .hero-bg element itself becomes transparent to pointer events.
